questions.markdown:
Which data structure directly supports undoing the most recent action first?

**(A)** Queue

**(B)** Stack

**(C)** Sorted array

**(D)** Adjacency matrix
reviewNotes: Endsem Papers: theory questions adapted from existing Manipal papers, with five newly authored MCQs on selected topics. Worked solutions are AI-authored and computationally checked where applicable.
questions.preparedSolution: **Correct option: (B).** A stack removes the most recently pushed action first (LIFO).

questions.markdown:
Edits A, B and C are pushed in that order onto an undo stack. Which edit does the first undo remove?

**(A)** A

**(B)** B

**(C)** All three

**(D)** C
reviewNotes: Endsem Papers: theory questions adapted from existing Manipal papers, with five newly authored MCQs on selected topics. Worked solutions are AI-authored and computationally checked where applicable.
questions.preparedSolution: **Correct option: (D).** C is the most recent edit and is at the top of the stack.

questions.markdown:
After edits A, B and C, two undo operations transfer actions to a redo stack. What is the redo stack from bottom to top?

**(A)** C, B

**(B)** B, C

**(C)** A, B

**(D)** A, C
reviewNotes: Endsem Papers: theory questions adapted from existing Manipal papers, with five newly authored MCQs on selected topics. Worked solutions are AI-authored and computationally checked where applicable.
questions.preparedSolution: **Correct option: (A).** The first undo pushes C onto redo; the second pushes B above C.

questions.markdown:
The redo stack contains C, B from bottom to top. Which edit is reapplied by one redo operation?

**(A)** A

**(B)** C

**(C)** B

**(D)** Both B and C
reviewNotes: Endsem Papers: theory questions adapted from existing Manipal papers, with five newly authored MCQs on selected topics. Worked solutions are AI-authored and computationally checked where applicable.
questions.preparedSolution: **Correct option: (C).** Redo pops the top action, B, and puts it back on undo.

questions.markdown:
In a conventional two-stack editor, what happens to the redo stack when a new edit is made after an undo?

**(A)** It is reversed

**(B)** It is cleared

**(C)** It is unchanged

**(D)** It becomes the undo stack
reviewNotes: Endsem Papers: theory questions adapted from existing Manipal papers, with five newly authored MCQs on selected topics. Worked solutions are AI-authored and computationally checked where applicable.
questions.preparedSolution: **Correct option: (B).** A new edit starts a new editing branch, so the previously undone future actions are discarded.

questions.preparedSolution:
Calls push frames in this order: main, fun2, fun1. Returns remove frames in the reverse order: fun1, fun2, main. The output is:

    Inside fun1
    Inside fun2
    Inside main

A frame holds the return address, parameters, local variables and saved execution state as required by the calling convention. A queue would remove the oldest caller first, although that caller is suspended awaiting its callee, so it does not represent normal nested call/return order.
